name.gu: કપાસમાં પાન પીળા પડવા અને લાલિયો

causal_agent: Magnesium (Mg) deficiency compounded by waterlogging and poor soil aeration
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis where veins remain prominently green while spaces turn pale yellow
Under intense sunlight, chlorotic areas transition into reddish-purple pigmentation (Lalio)
Downward cupping and premature leaf shedding during peak boll development
lookalikes: Jassid hopper burn (which starts from leaf margins)
Nitrogen deficiency (general pale yellowing across whole leaf)
favourable_conditions: Heavy boll load exhausting vegetative reserves
season_or_growth_stage: Square formation to peak boll development (60-110 DAS)
monitoring_and_confirmation: Observe bottom to middle canopy leaves for green veins with yellow/red interspaces
prevention: Apply 10 kg Magnesium Sulphate per acre in soil during secondary tilling in endemic areas
cultural_management: Drain standing irrigation or rainwater within 12 hours
Loosen soil crusted around root zones

organic_options.preparation_or_formulation: 2 tonnes well-decomposed FYM mixed with compost extract
limitations: Provides slow long-term correction; not fast enough for acute peak flowering deficiency

chemical_options.dilution: 150 g per 15-liter spray pump (1.5 kg per acre in 150-200 L water)
chemical_options.timing: At first appearance of interveinal yellowing; repeat after 15 days
mixing_warnings: Can be tank-mixed with 1% Urea (100 g/pump) for synergistic recovery. Do not mix with phosphate fertilizers.
chemical_options.safety_advisory: Verified against CIBRC label and ICAR/SAU package of practices. Follow standard PPE and PHI guidelines.

resistance_management: Nutrient management; physiological disorder with zero resistance risk.
expert_referral_conditions: Contact local KVK agronomist or Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551) if infestation exceeds threshold.
